question: Through which openings does cerebrospinal fluid leave the fourth ventricle to flow around the outside of the brain?

options.A: Internal carotid canals
options.B: Cerebral aqueduct channels
options.C: Median and lateral apertures
options.D: Interventricular foramina

explanation: Well done! The median and lateral apertures act like exit doors in the fourth ventricle, letting fluid flow out into the subarachnoid space.

question: Which piece of personal protective equipment is put on last when preparing for a sterile procedure?

options.A: Cap
options.B: Gloves
options.C: Gown
options.D: Mask

explanation: Gloves are always donned last so they remain clean and do not touch other equipment during the gowning and masking process. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h5)

question: Which professionals typically make up the multidisciplinary mental health team?

options.A: Surgeons, dentists, and hospital accountants
options.B: Lab technicians and administrative secretaries
options.C: Nurses, psychiatrists, social workers, and occupational therapists
options.D: Pharmacists and hospital security guards only

explanation: A comprehensive mental health team includes various specialists working together to address different recovery needs. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h7)

question: What is a great natural food source of folic acid?

options.A: Refined white sugar
options.B: Pasteurized whole milk
options.C: Green leafy vegetables
options.D: Processed red meat

explanation: Green leafy veggies like ugu, spinach, and bitter leaf are absolute powerhouses for natural folate. Eat your greens!

question: A clinic has funds to build either a new youth center or a borehole for clean water. A community diagnosis shows high rates of waterborne diseases. What should be funded first?

options.A: Both projects equally, regardless of the community health data
options.B: The youth center, because young people complain the loudest
options.C: Neither project, until the national government gives more money
options.D: The borehole, because it addresses the identified health crisis

explanation: Resources must be directed toward solving the specific health threats uncovered during the diagnostic assessment. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the medical term for the exaggerated inward curve of the lower back seen in pregnancy?

options.A: Cervical subluxation
options.B: Compensatory lumbar lordosis
options.C: Thoracic scoliosis
options.D: Lateral kyphosis

explanation: Lordosis is just the natural inward curve of the lower back. During pregnancy, it becomes more pronounced (exaggerated) to help balance out the heavy bump.

question: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks presents with a severe headache, blurred vision, and high blood pressure. What condition should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Postpartum depression
options.C: Pre-eclampsia
options.D: Placenta previa

explanation: High blood pressure combined with visual disturbances and severe headaches during pregnancy are classic warning signs of pre-eclampsia. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T015#GNS226_U1_T015_h2)

question: Where does the circulating nurse work during a surgical procedure?

options.A: Outside the sterile field, managing room coordination and documentation
options.B: Inside the sterile field, handling surgical instruments directly
options.C: In the hospital pharmacy preparing medications
options.D: In the recovery ward away from the surgical suite

explanation: Well done! The circulating nurse stays unscrubbed and moves around outside the sterile zone to coordinate and handle records.

question: What does the term ' hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy' mean?

options.A: Brain injury resulting from lack of oxygen and blood flow
options.B: A chronic skin rash caused by poor circulation
options.C: Sudden kidney failure due to low fluid volume
options.D: An infection of the lining surrounding the lungs

explanation: Break it down: 'hypoxic' (low oxygen), 'ischemic' (low blood flow), 'encephalopathy' (brain disease/injury). You've mastered a big medical term!

question: Why does the brain cut back on its own chemical receptors after repeated drug use?

options.A: To increase the speed of normal digestion
options.B: To store extra energy for physical exercise
options.C: To improve overall visual acuity at night
options.D: To protect itself from chemical overload

explanation: Well thought out! When a drug floods the brain, it tries to protect itself by reducing receptors (down-regulation) to restore some balance. The body is always trying to keep things stable!

question: A patient is rushed in unconscious, with very tiny pupils (pinpoint) and slow, shallow breathing. What type of poison do you suspect?

options.A: Stimulants
options.B: Anticholinergics
options.C: Opioids
options.D: Household bleach

explanation: You nailed it! Pinpoint pupils combined with depressed breathing are the classic textbook signs of an opioid overdose.

question: Why is stomach cancer often found at a late stage?

options.A: Diagnostic imaging tests cannot visualize the inner stomach lining.
options.B: Tumors in the stomach grow much faster than in any other organ.
options.C: Early symptoms closely mimic common, benign stomach issues like gastritis.
options.D: Patients routinely refuse endoscopy procedures until they bleed.

explanation: Exactly! Because early signs look just like normal heartburn or mild gastritis, people often brush it off until the tumor grows larger.

question: Which of the following is one of the famous 'five rights' of clinical delegation?

options.A: Right ward location
options.B: Right circumstance
options.C: Right financial cost
options.D: Right shift timing

explanation: Always remember the five rights: right task, right circumstance, right person, right direction, and right supervision!

question: What causes the movement called restitution right after the baby's head is born?

options.A: The shoulders push past the perineum simultaneously
options.B: The mother pushes extra hard to clear the airway
options.C: The midwife manually turns the baby to check for breathing
options.D: The head untwists to realign with the shoulders inside the pelvis

explanation: Brilliant! Restitution is just the head naturally untwisting and straightening out with the shoulders after it pops out.

question: In the ABCDE primary survey, what does the letter 'D' stand for?

options.A: Disability
options.B: Diagnosis
options.C: Drainage
options.D: Dehydration

explanation: D is for Disability! It is just a quick check of the patient's neurological status and brain function.

question: What is an absolute must-have medication every midwife must carry for the third stage of labor?

options.A: Intravenous general anesthesia
options.B: Magnesium sulfate for chronic cough
options.C: Oxytocin for hemorrhage prevention
options.D: Broad-spectrum oral antibiotics

explanation: Oxytocin is your best friend after the baby is delivered! It helps the womb contract and stops heavy bleeding.

question: Why is it helpful to ask about the exact kind of pain a patient has, like whether it feels burning or sharp?

options.A: It proves to the medical team that the patient is telling the truth
options.B: It is required by hospital insurance companies before giving drugs
options.C: It prevents the patient from feeling anxious about their diagnosis
options.D: It helps identify the underlying cause, like nerve or bone involvement

explanation: Different types of pain need different medicines—for instance, nerve pain often requires special drugs alongside standard painkillers.

question: When planning a study, what exactly is a research design?

options.A: The overall structural blueprint for conducting a study
options.B: A detailed biography of the principal investigator
options.C: The final bibliography list at the end of a thesis
options.D: The statistical software used to type the report

explanation: Spot on! The research design is your master plan that guides you step-by-step from start to finish.

question: How can you tell if a patient has a typical post-dural puncture headache?

options.A: It only hurts when the patient eats or drinks
options.B: It disappears completely when the room is dark
options.C: It gets worse when the patient sits or stands up
options.D: It stays the exact same intensity all day long

explanation: You nailed it! These headaches get worse when upright because of lower fluid pressure around the brain, and they feel better when lying flat.

question: Why must a nurse evaluate both the urinary and reproductive systems together?

options.A: Patients cannot distinguish between urinary and reproductive pain
options.B: Issues in one system often directly affect the other
options.C: The anatomical structures share the exact same nerve supply
options.D: Hospital policies mandate performing both exams simultaneously

explanation: Because the urinary and reproductive systems share close anatomical proximity and pathways, pathology in one frequently impacts the other. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T2#GNS213_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why do nurses encourage new mothers to walk around soon after delivery (early ambulation)?

options.A: To completely eliminate white blood cells from circulation
options.B: To stimulate the kidneys to stop producing erythropoietin
options.C: To help prevent dangerous blood clots in the deep veins
options.D: To immediately restore the pre-pregnancy plasma volume

explanation: Get those legs moving! Walking helps blood circulate properly and stops clots from forming in the legs after birth.

question: Which maneuver is standardly used to open the airway of an unresponsive patient without a neck injury?

options.A: Head-tilt, chin-lift maneuver
options.B: Jaw-thrust maneuver
options.C: Chest compression sweep
options.D: Recovery position roll

explanation: The head-tilt, chin-lift lifts the tongue away from the back of the throat to clear the airway. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why is it important for nurses to use standard nutritional terms?

options.A: It allows nurses to cook meals for patients.
options.B: It prevents dangerous misunderstandings among the healthcare team.
options.C: It completely replaces the need for blood tests.
options.D: It speeds up the hospital discharge process.

explanation: Great job! Using clear, standard words means doctors, nurses, and dietitians are all on the same page, keeping your patients safe.

question: Which contraceptive category offers protection against both pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Subdermal implants
options.B: Barrier methods
options.C: Copper intrauterine devices
options.D: Progestin mini-pills

explanation: Barrier methods like condoms physically block bodily fluids, thereby preventing the transmission of infectious organisms as well as sperm. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h5)

question: What is the main danger of failing to document a medication right after giving it?

options.A: Another nurse might assume it was not given and accidentally administer a dangerous duplicate dose.
options.B: The patient's identification card will automatically expire.
options.C: The hospital pharmacy will run out of stock within twenty-four hours.
options.D: The patient will immediately experience a severe allergic reaction.

explanation: Always chart your meds immediately! If it isn't written down, the next nurse on duty might think the patient missed a dose and give it again by mistake.

question: What is the recommended duration for exclusive breastfeeding according to health guidelines?

options.A: First two weeks of life
options.B: Throughout the entire first year
options.C: First six months of life
options.D: Only until solid foods are desired at month two

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding provides all necessary nutrients and protective antibodies for the first six months of an infant's life. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h6)

question: Why do dietitians need to understand human behavior along with food science?

options.A: Food chemistry changes completely based on the patient's mood
options.B: Patients need to feel understood in their cultural and personal habits to follow meal plans
options.C: Biochemical data alone is enough to change eating habits permanently
options.D: Psychological evaluations are legally required before writing a hospital diet

explanation: Knowing the science of food is only half the battle! If a patient's personal or cultural beliefs clash with the diet, they won't be able to follow it.

question: What is the best diagnostic test for looking directly at stomach ulcers and taking tiny tissue samples?

options.A: Plain abdominal X-ray
options.B: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy
options.C: Barium swallow radiography
options.D: Abdominal ultrasound

explanation: Well done! Passing a tiny camera down (endoscopy) lets the doctor see the stomach lining directly and take samples for tests.

question: When lifting an object from the floor, how should a patient position their back?

options.A: Twisted to one side for better balance
options.B: Straight, by bending at the knees and hips
options.C: Curved forward tightly to reach the item
options.D: Arching backward as far as possible

explanation: Bending the knees and keeping the back straight protects the spinal discs from injury during lifting. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h4)

question: Why does the conjunctiva become easily inflamed during an infection?

options.A: It lacks any form of blood supply
options.B: It is directly exposed to the external environment
options.C: It produces thick, sticky tears
options.D: It contains heavy layers of bone

explanation: Because the conjunctiva lines the exposed outer surface of the eye and inner eyelids, it readily catches dust, germs, and allergens. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which cranial nerve controls how we move our tongue for talking and swallowing?

options.A: Hypoglossal nerve
options.B: Trochlear nerve
options.C: Accessory nerve
options.D: Abducens nerve

explanation: Well done! Cranial Nerve XII is the hypoglossal nerve, and it gives our tongue muscles the power to move smoothly.

question: Why should cancer pain medication be given on a regular schedule rather than only when the patient asks?

options.A: It ensures the prescription bottle lasts for the full prescribed month.
options.B: It prevents the patient from developing a physical addiction to the drugs.
options.C: It maintains a steady blood level of medication to prevent severe pain from returning.
options.D: It reduces the risk of experiencing common gastrointestinal side effects.

explanation: Scheduled dosing keeps pain under control before it gets too intense. It's much easier to prevent pain than to chase it once it spikes!

question: Which of these is NOT a common trigger for a sickle cell pain crisis?

options.A: Dehydration from drinking too little water
options.B: An underlying viral or bacterial infection
options.C: Exposure to sudden cold weather environments
options.D: Eating a diet high in green leafy vegetables

explanation: Green leafy vegetables are healthy and safe! Infections, cold weather, and not drinking enough water are the real troublemakers that trigger a painful crisis.

question: Why is it important to report medication near-misses and errors through institutional incident reporting systems?

options.A: It helps the healthcare team identify systemic flaws to prevent future harm
options.B: It allows the pharmacy to bill the insurance company for wasted drugs
options.C: It ensures that negligent nurses are immediately fired from the facility
options.D: It provides legal protection for the hospital during malpractice lawsuits

explanation: Reporting errors highlights weak spots in the medication system so safety procedures can be improved. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical emotional response when a patient faces a permanent disability?

options.A: Grief over the loss of physical function
options.B: Anxiety about the future and financial strain
options.C: Depression due to lifestyle changes
options.D: Immediate and permanent acceptance without any sadness

explanation: Adapting to a disability is a complex emotional journey that usually involves shock, denial, and grief before acceptance is reached. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h7)

question: How many major components typically make up a comprehensive neurological assessment?

options.A: Eight
options.B: Twelve
options.C: Two
options.D: Five

explanation: The standard exam covers mental status, cranial nerves, motor system, sensory system, and reflexes. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which body system is in charge of releasing the hormones that trigger puberty?

options.A: The urinary system
options.B: The endocrine system
options.C: The respiratory system
options.D: The lymphatic system

explanation: Spot on! The endocrine system is made up of glands that send hormones straight into your bloodstream to guide important body changes like puberty.

question: What is the primary focus of non-pain symptom management in palliative care?

options.A: Speeding up the natural dying process safely
options.B: Curing the underlying terminal disease process
options.C: Eliminating the need for any medications
options.D: Maximizing patient comfort and quality of life

explanation: Palliative care focuses on comfort and quality of life when a cure is no longer possible. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h1)

question: What is the main goal of cost containment in a nursing unit?

options.A: Stopping all purchases of new clinical technology permanently
options.B: Reducing unnecessary expenses without harming patient care quality
options.C: Firing experienced nurses to hire cheaper untrained workers
options.D: Cutting all spending on patient medications to maximize profit

explanation: Cost containment is about cutting waste and saving money while making sure patient safety and care quality remain top-notch.

question: Why do doctors often add epinephrine to the local numbing medicine for a skin biopsy?

options.A: To constrict blood vessels and reduce bleeding
options.B: To neutralize acidic pH levels in the local tissue
options.C: To completely eliminate the initial stinging sensation
options.D: To speed up the healing time of the skin wound

explanation: Epinephrine makes blood vessels temporarily narrow (vasoconstriction), which keeps the workspace nice and clear of blood and helps the numbing medicine last longer.

question: What is the main goal of placing the harvested skin sample into normal saline or water?

options.A: To sterilize the sample from any surface bacterial contamination
options.B: To encourage the microfilariae to emerge out into the fluid
options.C: To dissolve the tissue completely so only DNA remains
options.D: To preserve the tissue for permanent paraffin embedding

explanation: Spot on! The liquid tricks the live microfilariae into crawling right out of the skin snippet so we can spot them under the microscope.

question: Which of these is a red-flag sign of a severe allergic reaction that needs instant emergency help?

options.A: Sudden facial swelling and difficulty breathing
options.B: Faint drowsiness after taking a nighttime sedative
options.C: Slight urine discoloration from a vitamin supplement
options.D: Mild dry mouth lasting for two hours

explanation: Trouble breathing and swollen lips mean anaphylaxis. That is an all-hands-on-deck emergency in the ward!

question: Why do cancer drugs (cytotoxic drugs) cause hair loss and upset stomachs?

options.A: The drugs accumulate exclusively in the skin
options.B: Healthy cells actively absorb the toxins
options.C: These healthy tissues also divide rapidly
options.D: The immune system attacks the medicine

explanation: Great thinking! Because these drugs target fast division, they accidentally affect normal body parts that also grow quickly, like hair roots and stomach lining.

question: A study shows a new sleep aid helps patients fall asleep 2 minutes faster, backed by strong math (p = 0.001). What should a nurse consider next?

options.A: Whether the study used an independent t-test instead of an ANOVA test
options.B: Whether the p-value is too high to trust the results of the research paper
options.C: Whether the null hypothesis was accidentally proven to be completely true
options.D: Whether saving 2 minutes is clinically meaningful enough to justify changing routines

explanation: Brilliant thinking! Even with great statistics, as nurses we always ask: does this tiny numerical change actually make a worthwhile difference for our patients?

question: Which skin sign strongly points to a liver problem or high bilirubin levels?

options.A: Pallor
options.B: Petechiae
options.C: Cyanosis
options.D: Jaundice

explanation: Jaundice gives the skin and eyes a yellowish tint because bilirubin is building up in the body.

question: What is the true relationship between FGM and major world religions?

options.A: Christian scriptures require the procedure for moral purity
options.B: FGM is a cultural practice falsely linked to religious texts
options.C: The Holy Quran explicitly commands all families to perform FGM
options.D: Islamic law strictly forbids any form of traditional surgery

explanation: Well done! Major religious books do not command FGM—the link is just a cultural misconception.

question: What hormone drives the growth of an ER-positive breast cancer tumor?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Cortisol
options.D: Estrogen

explanation: ER stands for Estrogen Receptor! ER-positive tumors have these receptors on their surface and use estrogen like fuel to grow and multiply. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h4)

question: Which of the following is a direct health function of the PTA?

options.A: Stocking the school clinic with first aid materials
options.B: Performing surgical operations during emergencies
options.C: Prescribing antibiotics to sick students in class
options.D: Teaching all the mathematics lessons in school

explanation: Providing basic first aid supplies is a practical way the PTA helps manage minor health issues in school. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h2)

question: A nurse arrives in a new village to start a malaria project. What should she do FIRST?

options.A: Order the demolition of stagnant water pools near the houses
options.B: Distribute mosquito nets to the first people she meets on the road
options.C: Set up a treatment table in the market square and wait for patients
options.D: Visit the village chief and key community leaders to introduce herself

explanation: Proper community entry requires meeting leadership and building rapport before taking any health action. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why does a person trapped in a smoke-filled room suffer from asphyxia?

options.A: Severe dehydration and low blood volume
options.B: Toxic gas inhalation replacing ambient oxygen
options.C: Allergic reaction to dust particles
options.D: Sudden paralysis of the heart muscle

explanation: Thick smoke and poisonous gases take up all the space in the air, pushing out the good oxygen your lungs need to function.

question: On a full blood count lab report, what does the abbreviation MCV stand for?

options.A: Minimum capillary vessel
options.B: Measured cellular viscosity
options.C: Mean corpuscular volume
options.D: Maximum clotting velocity

explanation: MCV tells us the average size of the red blood cells. It's super helpful for figuring out what kind of anaemia a patient has!

question: A nursing mother refuses to take her sick child to the clinic because the nearest facility is across a flooded river with no bridge. What primary factor is affecting her health behaviour?

options.A: A lack of personal intelligence
options.B: Stubborn defiance against modern medicine
options.C: An allergic reaction to clinic drugs
options.D: Structural and environmental barriers

explanation: This isn't about her willingness—it's a physical hurdle! Bad roads, long distances, and missing bridges are structural and environmental challenges. You're learning to look at the bigger picture in public health.

question: What is the primary focus of gender equality?

options.A: Treating patients differently based on their economic class
options.B: Ensuring all genders have the exact same rights and opportunities
options.C: Providing extra resources exclusively to marginalized groups
options.D: Ignoring biological differences during physical health exams

explanation: Equality focuses on giving everyone the same starting point and identical access to resources and rights. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why do nurse researchers set up a conceptual framework before collecting data?

options.A: To replace the need for a formal literature review
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of conducting the study
options.C: To guarantee that the study gets published immediately
options.D: To make sense of complex human experiences and guide the inquiry

explanation: Research can get messy! A good framework helps you organize your thoughts and makes sure you look at all the important parts of a tricky problem.

question: Why is long-term evaluation so important in Behaviour Change Communication?

options.A: It proves that the nurse worked extra hours without taking a break
options.B: It measures whether actual health practices were sustained over time
options.C: It allows the hospital to increase consultation fees for patients
options.D: It replaces the need for daily clinical nursing assessments

explanation: You nailed it! Real habit changes take time. Long-term checks let you know if the community kept up the healthy lifestyle weeks or months later.

question: What is the primary purpose of a thoracocentesis?

options.A: To remove fluid or air from the pleural space
options.B: To measure the exact pressure inside the heart
options.C: To deliver oxygen directly into the lung tissue
options.D: To clear thick mucus blockages from the main bronchi

explanation: Thoracocentesis involves entering the pleural space to drain abnormal collections of fluid or air that compress the lung. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h1)

question: When a patient uses a single-point cane for walking, which hand should hold the cane?

options.A: The hand on the stronger side
options.B: The hand on the weaker side
options.C: Both hands must hold the handle
options.D: Whichever hand is most dominant

explanation: Holding the cane on the strong side allows the patient to lean weight onto it while moving the opposite weak leg forward. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h3)

question: A patient with an untreated collapsed lung (pneumothorax) is booked for a flight. What should be done first?

options.A: Decompress or treat the condition before takeoff
options.B: Fly at a much higher altitude to cure the air pocket
options.C: Remove all supplemental oxygen from the patient
options.D: Proceed with immediate takeoff without any changes

explanation: You nailed it! Remember Boyle's law? Trapped air expands as you go higher, so a pneumothorax must be treated *before* takeoff to prevent a life-threatening crisis.

question: What is the primary driving factor behind gender-based violence in most societies?

options.A: Sudden economic inflation within households
options.B: A lack of religious devotion in the community
options.C: Unequal power relations and patriarchal norms
options.D: Genetic predispositions toward aggressive behavior

explanation: GBV is deeply driven by structural inequalities and cultural beliefs that promote dominance and control over specific genders. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h1)

question: Which meningeal layer wraps around the brain so tightly that it dips into every single groove and fold?

options.A: Dura mater
options.B: Arachnoid mater
options.C: Periosteal layer
options.D: Pia mater

explanation: You got it! The pia mater is soft and tender, clinging closely to every curve of the brain like a second skin.

question: What is the main purpose of using a partograph during intrapartum care?

options.A: To test the mother's blood sugar levels
options.B: To register the baby's name after birth
options.C: To calculate the total cost of hospital delivery
options.D: To monitor the progress of labor and detect problems early

explanation: The partograph is a visual tool used by nurses and midwives to track labor progress and maternal-fetal well-being. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h4)

question: What does holistic nursing care require nurses to address alongside physical needs?

options.A: Spiritual and emotional needs
options.B: Financial planning records
options.C: Dietary supplement costs
options.D: Legal guardianship papers

explanation: Holistic nursing looks at the entire person, which includes physical, emotional, and spiritual dimensions of health. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T13#GNS225_U5_T13_h1)

question: What does accountability mean when a registered nurse delegates a task?

options.A: The nursing assistant takes all legal blame if something goes wrong
options.B: The registered nurse remains ultimately responsible for the patient outcome
options.C: Nobody is responsible once the task is handed over to staff
options.D: The hospital management assumes all blame for delegation errors

explanation: While responsibility for doing the task is transferred, the registered nurse retains final accountability for supervising and ensuring patient safety. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h6)

question: What does 'intrinsic sphincter deficiency' mean?

options.A: Blockage of urine flow by the prostate gland
options.B: Damage or weakness of the urethral sphincter muscle itself
options.C: A temporary infection lining the urinary tract
options.D: Overactivity of the main bladder muscle

explanation: Simply put, the valve muscle itself has lost some of its strength and can no longer seal tightly on its own.

question: While looking at an ovary slide under a microscope, you spot a large fluid-filled space called an antrum. What kind of follicle is this?

options.A: Primordial follicle
options.B: Tertiary follicle
options.C: Atretic follicle
options.D: Primary follicle

explanation: You're doing great. That fluid-filled space (antrum) is the classic giveaway that you are looking at a mature or tertiary follicle.

question: What do we mean by 'second victim syndrome' in healthcare?

options.A: A secondary illness caught by a patient while staying in the ward
options.B: Emotional trauma experienced by a clinician after being involved in an error
options.C: The legal penalty given to a hospital following a malpractice lawsuit
options.D: The family member who has to pay extra hospital bills for an injury

explanation: Nurses and doctors who go through a tough adverse event often carry deep emotional pain. We call them the second victims.

question: Why should you advise a client NOT to massage her arm or buttock after a DMPA injection?

options.A: It pushes the liquid medicine directly into a blood vessel
options.B: It speeds up drug absorption and shortens protection
options.C: It stops the needle puncture wound from closing properly
options.D: It causes severe bruising on the skin surface

explanation: Massaging increases blood flow, making the body absorb the hormone too fast. That means it might wear off sooner than expected!

question: A nurse walks into a ward and finds a junior colleague throwing a used syringe into a regular black polythene bag. What is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Correct the colleague immediately and ensure the syringe is moved to the sharps box
options.B: Ignore the mistake because cleaners will sort it out later anyway
options.C: Write an official query letter to the hospital medical director
options.D: Remove all waste bins from the ward to teach everyone a lesson

explanation: Nurses have a duty to correct segregation errors instantly to maintain a safe working and clinical environment. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h7)

question: What is most important when creating health education posters for a rural Nigerian community?

options.A: Ensuring every poster costs very little to print
options.B: Writing the text exclusively in advanced medical English
options.C: Featuring foreign medical experts on the cover page
options.D: Using local languages and familiar cultural imagery

explanation: For health messages to stick, people need to see themselves in the pictures and understand the language without struggling. Keep it relatable! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h5)

question: What is a big perk of having a 'flat' organizational structure in a hospital ward?

options.A: Orders take longer to reach the bedside staff
options.B: It completely removes the need for a head nurse
options.C: It creates more promotion posts for middle managers
options.D: Staff nurses can communicate more directly with top leadership

explanation: Spot on! By cutting out excess middle management, the distance between the bedside nurse and upper management shrinks, making communication much faster.

question: Which imaging test uses a strong magnetic field instead of X-rays to picture soft tissues?

options.A: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.B: Cerebral angiography
options.C: Plain skull X-ray
options.D: Computed tomography scan

explanation: MRI uses powerful magnets and radio waves to create detailed pictures without using X-rays.

question: A patient doing a 24-hour urine collection tells you they accidentally flushed one sample halfway through the day. What should you do?

options.A: Discard the current collection and restart the entire 24-hour process
options.B: Estimate the missed amount and add extra water to make up the volume
options.C: Extend the collection period by twelve hours to make up for the loss
options.D: Send the incomplete jug to the lab with a note explaining the lost sample

explanation: Ah, frustration! But a 24-hour test has to be complete. Missing even one bathroom trip means the numbers won't be accurate, so it's best to start fresh another day.

question: A surgical drain was flowing nicely, but now it has suddenly stopped. What should you suspect first?

options.A: The body has miraculously stopped producing all normal inflammatory fluid
options.B: The collection container is now completely sterile and safe to remove
options.C: The surgical wound has finished healing completely on its own
options.D: The tube might be blocked or kinked inside or outside the patient

explanation: When output stops abruptly, don't assume a miracle healing! Always check the tubing first for a clot, mucus, or a pesky kink.

question: How do local farmers directly support school feeding initiatives?

options.A: By teaching science classes on agricultural botany
options.B: By prescribing nutritional supplements to sick children
options.C: By supplying locally grown, nutritious food produce
options.D: By auditing the financial books of the school canteen

explanation: Local farmers provide fresh food ingredients, ensuring the feeding program is sustainable and utilizes local produce. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h6)

question: What does the social ecology framework primarily examine when studying adolescent health?

options.A: The genetic history passed down from parents to the child
options.B: The entire surrounding environment and social network of the teenager
options.C: The specific biological changes happening during puberty
options.D: The financial status of the local healthcare facility

explanation: Social ecology looks at how multiple layers of a person's social environment interact to influence their overall health and behavior. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T20#GNS312_U3_T20_h1)

question: How does poorly controlled diabetes mellitus make a patient more likely to catch infections?

options.A: High blood sugar levels create a favorable environment for pathogen growth and impair white blood cell function
options.B: It permanently destroys the skin, removing the body's primary mechanical barrier to the outside world
options.C: It causes immediate and total depletion of the body's red blood cell count
options.D: It forces the liver to produce antibodies that mistakenly attack healthy internal organs

explanation: Spot on! High sugar acts like food for germs, while making it harder for white blood cells to do their job of fighting back. Keep up the great work!

question: Besides eating healthy food, what is the big benefit of practicing portion control?

options.A: Maintaining energy balance and preventing excessive weight gain
options.B: Ensuring that digestion takes place only during nighttime hours
options.C: Eliminating the need to consume any carbohydrates at all
options.D: Reducing the body's overall requirement for clean drinking water

explanation: Exactly. Portion control stops us from taking in more energy than we burn off, helping us stay at a healthy weight.

question: Why is a teamwork (multidisciplinary) approach important for older adults' mental healthcare?

options.A: It allows the hospital to discharge the patient much faster
options.B: It addresses the complex physical, emotional, and social needs of the patient
options.C: It ensures that nurses do not have to interact with the patient's family
options.D: It eliminates the need for any kind of medication therapy

explanation: Older patients often have medical, social, and emotional needs all at once, requiring different experts to team up. Teamwork makes the dream work!

question: Which of these is NOT a goal of a strong healthcare referral network?

options.A: Isolating the client from all family and friends
options.B: Ensuring continuity of medical follow-up
options.C: Providing access to professional social workers
options.D: Connecting the client with community support groups

explanation: Good referral networks are designed to build a strong safety net and reduce isolation, never to cut a client off from the people who love and support them. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h7)

question: What is the specific name of the stress ulcer that forms in the stomach due to severe burn trauma?

options.A: Zollinger-Ellison ulcer
options.B: Cushing's ulcer
options.C: Peptic ulcer
options.D: Curling's ulcer

explanation: Think 'Curling' up from belly pain after a burn! It's a classic stress ulcer caused by low blood flow to the stomach early in shock.

question: Which of these shows a patient is having trouble with the ADL of 'transferring'?

options.A: The patient forgets to add sugar to their tea.
options.B: The patient cannot balance their monthly bills.
options.C: The patient wears mismatched socks and unbuttoned shirts.
options.D: The patient needs help moving from the bed to a chair.

explanation: Spot on! In nursing, 'transferring' is all about safely moving a patient from one surface to another, like from a bed to a wheelchair.

question: Why is it helpful to view drug addiction as a public health disease rather than a moral failure?

options.A: It encourages affected individuals to seek medical treatment earlier without fear
options.B: It allows the government to stop all funding for local hospitals
options.C: It guarantees that prescription drugs will become free for everyone
options.D: It stops people from ever feeling sad or stressed in life

explanation: Stigma makes people hide their struggles. Treating addiction as a medical issue helps patients come forward for help proudly and early.

question: Why is it important to note if a patient frequently strains during bowel movements?

options.A: Constipation directly damages the pudendal nerve roots in the lower spine
options.B: Bowel movements have no connection to pelvic floor health
options.C: Chronic straining places continuous downward pressure and stretches pelvic muscles
options.D: Straining causes the kidneys to produce excess urine

explanation: You nailed it! Pushing too hard over time stretches out those supportive muscles and fascia, weakening the whole sling.

question: Why do we routinely give iron and folic acid tablets to pregnant women?

options.A: To prevent iron-deficiency anemia and support fetal development
options.B: To completely eliminate morning sickness throughout the pregnancy
options.C: To speed up the onset of labor during the final week
options.D: To ensure the baby is born with a higher birth weight

explanation: A pregnant woman's body needs extra blood volume! Iron prevents anemia, and folate protects the baby's brain and spine development.

question: You are assessing a patient's abdomen and suspect peritonitis. Which physical sign would you expect to find?

options.A: A rigid, board-like abdomen
options.B: A soft, painless belly
options.C: Cool and moist skin on the arms
options.D: Increased bowel sounds everywhere

explanation: Brilliant! When the lining of the belly gets irritated by leaked digestive juices or stool, the muscle wall tightens up stiffly to protect itself. You're building solid assessment skills!

question: Which of the following is a classic physical sign of repeated abuse often seen during a nursing assessment?

options.A: Generalized joint swelling caused by normal aging processes
options.B: Clean surgical incisions from previous routine procedures
options.C: Bruises in various stages of healing across the body
options.D: Symmetrical rashes located strictly on the lower extremities

explanation: Different colors of bruises indicate injuries sustained at different times, which is a strong indicator of ongoing physical abuse. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h2)

question: What should the nurse check when inspecting the dressing after the procedure?

options.A: Whether the skin has turned a pale yellow color
options.B: If the adhesive tape is completely waterproof
options.C: Signs of bleeding, swelling, or fluid leakage
options.D: The exact temperature of the bandage material

explanation: Spot on! Regular site checks ensure any bleeding or fluid leakage is caught and managed early.

question: Why does the rest of the baby's body slide out so quickly once the shoulders are born?

options.A: Maternal adrenaline production peaks right before delivery
options.B: The trunk and limbs are narrower than the head and shoulders
options.C: The amniotic fluid acts as a lubricant for the lower body
options.D: Uterine contractions become ten times stronger at this exact moment

explanation: You nailed it! Once the widest parts (head and shoulders) are safely out, the rest of the body is much narrower and slips right through.

question: How does educating girls and women directly improve maternal health in a community?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for hospitals and clinics
options.B: It empowers women to recognize pregnancy danger signs and seek prompt medical care
options.C: It guarantees that every woman will become a qualified midwife
options.D: It prevents women from ever getting pregnant

explanation: Education is powerful! When women understand health risks, they can spot danger early and make smart choices for themselves and their babies. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h3)

question: If you are calculating the incidence of a uterine infection, who belongs at the bottom (the denominator)?

options.A: Every single person living in the entire country
options.B: All children under the age of five years old
options.C: Only individuals with a uterus who are at risk
options.D: Only patients who already have the infection

explanation: Well done! The denominator should only include the people who are actually at risk of catching that specific condition.

question: Which statement best describes a coronary artery bypass graft operation?

options.A: A healthy vessel from elsewhere in the body is used to route blood around a blockage
options.B: A laser is passed through a neck vein to burn away the plaque inside the heart
options.C: Medication is injected directly into the heart wall to dissolve old scars
options.D: An artificial plastic heart is implanted to take over the work of the damaged organ

explanation: CABG surgery creates a new path for blood to travel by sewing a grafted vessel past the blocked section of the coronary artery. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h7)

question: Which body system does your skin belong to?

options.A: The integumentary system
options.B: The respiratory system
options.C: The circulatory system
options.D: The endocrine system

explanation: You got it! The skin is part of the integumentary system, which also includes your hair, nails, and glands that keep your body safe. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care in the final stages of an inherited degenerative disorder?

options.A: Testing family members for the presence of the gene
options.B: Finding a new experimental cure to reverse the disease
options.C: Maximizing comfort, managing pain, and preserving dignity
options.D: Increasing physical therapy sessions to restore lost muscle

explanation: Palliative care prioritizes comfort, relieving symptoms, and providing emotional support when life expectancy is limited.

question: An infant receives a vaccine four weeks too early. What is the correct nursing action?

options.A: Perform a blood test immediately to measure antibody levels
options.B: Administer a double dose at the next clinic visit to balance the schedule
options.C: Repeat the dose after the correct minimum interval has passed
options.D: Assume the child is fully protected and skip all future boosters

explanation: Doses given too early often don't count because the baby's system isn't quite ready or maternal antibodies block them. We simply repeat it at the right time to keep them safe.

question: What is the primary purpose of the cold chain in immunization?

options.A: To make sure syringes are sterile before an injection
options.B: To speed up the manufacturing process of new vaccines
options.C: To keep vaccines at the correct temperature until use
options.D: To freeze all vaccines solid for long-term transport

explanation: The cold chain ensures vaccines stay within safe temperature limits from the factory to the patient. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h1)

question: A nurse notices a husband is dominating the conversation and suspects his wife is hiding health issues. What is the best first step?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately and document that care was refused
options.B: Scold the husband in front of the patient for interrupting the health history
options.C: Refuse to let the husband enter the clinic room during future appointments
options.D: Create a moment to speak with the patient privately without the husband present

explanation: Always find a safe moment—like stepping out for a lab test or a quick bathroom break—to talk with the patient alone so she feels safe to share what's really going on.

question: What is the main difference between phantom limb sensation and phantom limb pain?

options.A: Pain only happens during the day, while sensation occurs exclusively while sleeping.
options.B: Sensation means the limb is still there, while pain means the nerve has died completely.
options.C: Pain is purely psychological, while sensation is caused by poor blood flow.
options.D: Sensation involves normal feelings like tingling, while pain involves burning or shooting hurt.

explanation: Phantom sensation is just a harmless awareness that the limb is missing (like feeling an itchy toe), whereas phantom pain is actual uncomfortable, shooting distress.

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do right after using a surgical instrument at the bedside?

options.A: Wipe away gross debris to prevent drying
options.B: Spray the metal with industrial lubricating oil
options.C: Place the item directly into an autoclave chamber
options.D: Submerge the instrument in concentrated bleach

explanation: Always do a quick pre-wipe! If blood and tissue dry onto the metal, they become ten times harder to clean later.

question: What is our best and most reliable guide when assessing a patient's pain?

options.A: The patient's own verbal report of the pain
options.B: The underlying surgical diagnosis on the chart
options.C: The family member's description of discomfort
options.D: The nurse's objective observation of vital signs

explanation: Pain is whatever the patient says it is! Because we can't feel it for them, their personal word is always our gold standard.

question: Your patient has a radial arterial line, and suddenly their hand looks pale, feels cold, and has a weak pulse. What is your very first step?

options.A: Apply a warm heating pad directly over the plastic catheter hub
options.B: Inflate the blood pressure cuff on that exact arm to high pressure
options.C: Document the finding as a normal reaction and check again in four hours
options.D: Notify the healthcare provider right away and assess distal circulation

explanation: That's a red flag for poor blood flow past the line! Whenever a limb turns cold and pale, you must act fast and alert the doctor to protect the tissue.

question: Which of these is a classic lung disease caused by breathing in mineral dust at work?

options.A: Cystic fibrosis
options.B: Silicosis
options.C: Acute bronchitis
options.D: Lobar pneumonia

explanation: Silicosis happens when workers breathe in tiny crystalline silica dust, often found in mining, construction, or masonry jobs.

question: What term describes the study of what the body does to a drug (absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion)?

options.A: Pharmacokinetics
options.B: Pharmacogenetics
options.C: Pharmacodynamics
options.D: Pharmaceutics

explanation: Nailed it! Pharmacokinetics tracks the journey of the drug through the body across those four famous ADME stages.

question: Which of the following should a nurse NOT do in end-of-life care?

options.A: Respecting the cultural and spiritual wishes of the family
options.B: Supporting the family through the grieving process
options.C: Withholding pain medication out of fear of addiction in a dying patient
options.D: Providing comfort measures and meticulous hygiene

explanation: Never hold back pain relief! At the end of life, our main duty is comfort. Addiction is not a worry when managing pain for a dying patient.

question: Why is inhalation therapy often preferred over oral medications for lung conditions?

options.A: It guarantees 100 percent absorption into the bloodstream
options.B: It works faster locally and reduces widespread side effects
options.C: It is completely free of any potential complications
options.D: It never requires patient coordination or special training

explanation: Targeting the lungs directly means smaller doses can treat the problem without affecting the rest of the body as heavily. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which sign around a surgical drain insertion site tells you an infection might be starting?

options.A: Normal skin color with slight firmness around the tube
options.B: Clear pink fluid on a dry, intact outer gauze
options.C: Foul-smelling pus and surrounding skin redness
options.D: A small drop of dried blood near the stitches

explanation: Spot on! Redness, warmth, swelling, and foul-smelling pus are classic signs that bacteria are multiplying. Time to alert the team!

question: A pregnant client at 32 weeks presents with sudden, painless vaginal bleeding, and an ultrasound shows her placenta is covering the cervix. What is this condition called?

options.A: Tubal ectopic pregnancy
options.B: Complete placental abruption
options.C: Spontaneous tubal abortion
options.D: Placenta previa

explanation: You got it! Placenta previa happens when the placenta implants low in the uterus and ends up covering the cervix. Great job connecting theory to real-world nursing care!

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to keep a stakeholder coalition strong and unified?

options.A: Mutual respect for different contributions
options.B: Clear roles for all participating members
options.C: Ignoring opposing views within the coalition
options.D: Transparent communication among groups

explanation: Spot on! Brushing opposing views under the rug destroys trust. A strong coalition needs open communication and respect for everyone's opinions.

question: What is the main thing that makes a research study 'non-experimental'?

options.A: The researcher does not manipulate the independent variable.
options.B: Random assignment is used for every participant.
options.C: A new treatment is tested against a placebo.
options.D: The study takes place only in a laboratory setting.

explanation: You've got this! In non-experimental studies, we simply watch and record things as they happen naturally, without changing or meddling with anything ourselves.

question: What does the 'thermic effect of food' mean?

options.A: Energy used to process and digest food
options.B: Heat produced when standing in cold weather
options.C: Calories burned during a heavy gym workout
options.D: Energy stored in fat tissue during starvation

explanation: Think of it this way: eating and digesting food actually makes your body work! The energy spent handling that food process is the thermic effect of food.

question: A bedridden patient has a red spot on their lower back that doesn't fade when pressed. As a nurse, what should you do first?

options.A: Implement a strict turning schedule and use a pressure-relieving surface
options.B: Restrict daily fluid intake to reduce local tissue edema
options.C: Apply strong antiseptic ointment directly over the red skin area
options.D: Massaged the reddened spot vigorously to stimulate blood flow

explanation: That red spot is an early pressure ulcer warning! Taking the pressure off by turning the patient is your best first move.

question: Which nutrient starts its chemical digestion in the oral cavity?

options.A: Triglycerides
options.B: Proteins
options.C: Vitamins
options.D: Carbohydrates

explanation: Salivary amylase is present in saliva and begins breaking down complex carbohydrates right inside the mouth. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h2)

question: Who usually develops tactical objectives in a healthcare organization?

options.A: Patients recovering in the inpatient wards
options.B: Middle managers like nurse managers and department heads
options.C: Maintenance staff fixing equipment in the basement
options.D: The top chief executive officer working alone

explanation: Department heads and nurse managers take broad executive goals and turn them into departmental action plans. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the medical term for when the tonsils get inflamed and swollen?

options.A: Laryngitis
options.B: Rhinitis
options.C: Tonsillitis
options.D: Pharyngitis

explanation: Correct! Tonsillitis simply means your tonsils are inflamed and fighting off an infection.

question: A researcher wants to study how nurses feel about working night shifts by having open conversations. Which data collection method is best?

options.A: Numerical blood pressure screening
options.B: In-depth qualitative interviews
options.C: A rigid multiple-choice questionnaire
options.D: Laboratory biomarker blood testing

explanation: Open-ended interviews are fantastic because they let nurses express their true feelings in their own words.

question: What is the single biggest preventable cause of chronic lung disease (COPD) worldwide?

options.A: Childhood asthma attacks
options.B: Inhaling coal dust at work
options.C: Smoke from indoor cooking fires
options.D: Tobacco smoke exposure

explanation: Tobacco smoke is tough on the airways and air sacs over time. Because people can choose to avoid or quit it, it stands out as the number one preventable cause of COPD globally.

question: In clinical communication, what does the acronym SBAR stand for?

options.A: System, Behavior, Analysis, Response
options.B: Symptoms, Blood, Airways, Respiration
options.C: Safety, Balance, Action, Review
options.D: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation

explanation: SBAR is a handy, structured tool nurses and doctors use to pass clear patient updates across quickly and safely.

question: What is the purpose of the acrosome sitting right at the head of a sperm cell?

options.A: Containing enzymes to help penetrate the egg during fertilization
options.B: Protecting the genetic material from the acidic vaginal environment
options.C: Generating ATP energy required for the movement of the tail
options.D: Housing the main metabolic machinery for protein synthesis

explanation: The acrosome is like a little tool kit filled with special enzymes that help the sperm break through the outer layers of an egg.

question: Why is the enforcement of anti-child marriage laws challenging in some parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Federal laws completely override all local traditions automatically
options.B: The coexistence of statutory, customary, and religious legal systems
options.C: Law enforcement agencies strictly monitor all private family homes
options.D: There are no documented cases of child marriage in urban areas

explanation: Because customary and religious laws often permit marriage at puberty or upon agreement by guardians, legal conflicts arise when federal acts are implemented. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h4)

question: How do progestin-only implants mainly prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By thickening cervical mucus, stopping ovulation, and thinning the endometrium
options.B: By increasing estrogen production to flush out the fertilized egg
options.C: By neutralizing male sperm cells directly inside the vaginal canal
options.D: By stimulating sudden contractions that empty the uterine cavity

explanation: Think of the progestin hormone as a triple-security system: it blocks sperm from entering, stops the ovary from releasing an egg, and makes the womb lining cozy-free for implantation!

question: What is the main purpose of doing a community health needs assessment?

options.A: To collect money from residents to build a private pharmacy
options.B: To fulfill government paperwork requirements without visiting the field
options.C: To discover actual health problems and disparities before planning action
options.D: To judge community members for poor hygiene practices

explanation: Exactly right! You have to know what's really going on before you can fix it. An assessment uncovers the true health challenges so you can target your help properly.

question: Which of these research questions is best answered with a quantitative design?

options.A: What is it like for a young mother to receive a diagnosis of breast cancer?
options.B: How do nurses emotionally experience the loss of a long-term patient?
options.C: Does a pre-operative education video reduce post-operative pain scores?
options.D: What meaning do elderly patients give to living in a nursing home?

explanation: Comparing pain scores before and after an intervention involves numbers and testing a hypothesis, which calls for quantitative research.

question: What is the main goal of public health surveillance for infectious diseases?

options.A: Ongoing collection and analysis of health data to guide public health action
options.B: Enforcing strict legal penalties for healthcare facilities that break sterile technique
options.C: Manufacture of safe and effective vaccines for global distribution
options.D: Providing emergency medical treatment to individual hospital patients

explanation: Correct! Tracking disease numbers helps public health teams spot trends and stop outbreaks early.

question: How does a provoked seizure differ from epilepsy?

options.A: Provoked seizures require lifelong anti-seizure medication
options.B: Provoked seizures occur due to a temporary, acute trigger like low blood sugar
options.C: Provoked seizures are always generalized tonic-clonic events
options.D: Provoked seizures only happen during sleep cycles

explanation: A provoked seizure happens because of a temporary stressor on the body, such as high fever or low blood sugar, rather than a chronic brain condition. Great job thinking it through!

question: Which of the following is an example of a long-acting reversible contraceptive (LARC) method?

options.A: Combined oral contraceptive pills
options.B: Subdermal contraceptive implants
options.C: Male latex barrier condoms
options.D: Spermicidal foaming vaginal tablets

explanation: Exactly! Implants and IUDs offer long-term protection against pregnancy, but can be easily removed whenever the client is ready.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common complication associated with tubal ligation surgery?

options.A: Permanent cessation of the menstrual cycle
options.B: Accidental injury to surrounding pelvic organs
options.C: Infection at the surgical incision site
options.D: Post-operative bleeding or hematoma formation

explanation: Tubal ligation does not stop menstrual periods because the ovaries remain untouched and continue to function normally. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h6)

question: Which group becomes the main guide for values, styles, and social behavior during the teenage years?

options.A: Community religious leaders
options.B: Primary school teachers
options.C: Peer groups
options.D: Extended family elders

explanation: Friends and peer groups heavily influence how teenagers dress, talk, and act as they search for where they fit in.

question: Why is the community health planning cycle described as continuous and circular?

options.A: The exact same health problem must be treated over and over again
options.B: Evaluation findings lead directly into the next round of assessment and planning
options.C: It must be repeated every thirty days regardless of community needs
options.D: Healthcare workers rotate through different villages in a fixed circle

explanation: Because health needs change and programs must adapt, the end of one evaluation simply sparks the beginning of the next planning phase. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h1)

question: What does cross-contamination mean in food safety?

options.A: The accidental freezing of fresh vegetables in the refrigerator
options.B: The mixing of two different dry grains in the same storage bin
options.C: The transfer of harmful germs from raw food to ready-to-eat food
options.D: The change in food color due to exposure to bright sunlight

explanation: Cross-contamination happens when bacteria move from raw items (like meat) to food you're about to eat without cooking.

question: A male patient appears quiet and defensive during his fertility workup. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Reassure him that male infertility is always easily cured with surgery
options.B: Provide a private, non-judgmental environment to discuss his concerns openly
options.C: Refer him immediately to a psychiatrist for severe clinical depression
options.D: Insist that his wife answers all the clinical questions for him

explanation: Creating a safe, supportive space helps lower defenses and encourages the patient to share his emotional burdens. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h8)

question: Why do some families prefer having FGM done by a healthcare worker instead of a traditional cutter?

options.A: Hospitals provide free reconstructive surgery
options.B: Traditional practitioners charge higher fees
options.C: They believe clinical settings make the procedure safe
options.D: The government mandates clinical procedures

explanation: Many families think that because it's done in a clinic with clean tools and pain relief, the harmful risks disappear. But medicalised FGM is still dangerous and harmful!

question: What does a major cross-match involve in the laboratory?

options.A: Mixing the donor's serum with the donor's own plasma
options.B: Checking the donor's white blood cell count under a microscope
options.C: Mixing the recipient's serum with the donor's red blood cells
options.D: Testing the recipient's urine for traces of breakdown proteins

explanation: The major cross-match checks if the patient's antibodies will attack the donor's red blood cells. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T8#GNS123_U2_T8_h5)

question: A patient refuses their home exercises and seems down. How should you view this as a nurse?

options.A: They clearly want their condition to deteriorate permanently
options.B: They are purposely wasting the healthcare team's valuable time
options.C: They have no right to question their prescribed care plan
options.D: They are likely overwhelmed and need support rather than judgment

explanation: When patients pull back, it's often burnout or emotional distress speaking. A little empathy goes a long way in helping them trust the process again.

question: Which of these is a vital disease-prevention shot routinely given during pregnancy clinics in Nigeria?

options.A: Insulin pump placement
options.B: Tetanus toxoid vaccination
options.C: Chemotherapy infusion
options.D: Joint replacement surgery

explanation: Well done! Tetanus toxoid is a routine life-saver given during pregnancy to protect both the mother and newborn baby from tetanus.

question: Why are our eyes so dependent on rod cells when we are trying to see in the dark?

options.A: Rods block out distracting light rays in dark rooms
options.B: Rods are located only in the front part of the cornea
options.C: Rods are extremely sensitive to low levels of light
options.D: Rods produce the pigments needed to see bright colors at night

explanation: Rods don't do color very well, but they are night-vision champions! They only need a tiny glimmer of light to help us spot shapes and shadows in the dark.

question: How is a physiological antagonist different from a regular receptor blocker?

options.A: It requires the destruction of the liver to take effect
options.B: It occurs only inside the digestive tract of animals
options.C: It always causes a permanent chemical bond in the blood
options.D: It uses separate receptors to produce opposite body effects

explanation: They don't fight over the same spot. Instead, they act on totally different receptors in the body, but their final effects cancel each other out—like a tug-of-war!

question: What is the main reason we give folic acid supplements in early pregnancy?

options.A: To stop maternal gestational hypertension
options.B: To prevent postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: To prevent neural tube defects
options.D: To increase daily breast milk production

explanation: Folic acid is a tiny pill with a huge job! It protects the baby's developing brain and spine right from the very start.

question: Which vaccine is routinely given during pregnancy to protect the newborn from a deadly infection?

options.A: Tetanus toxoid
options.B: Measles vaccine
options.C: Bacille Calmette-Guérin
options.D: Hepatitis A vaccine

explanation: Spot on! Tetanus toxoid is given to expectant mothers to protect their babies from neonatal tetanus. Great memory!

question: Which strategy works best for controlling rabies in local dog populations?

options.A: Mass animal vaccination campaigns
options.B: Daily antibiotic therapy for all puppies
options.C: Forced quarantine of infected human patients
options.D: Complete removal of all water sources

explanation: Vaccinating dogs builds up immunity across the animal population, stopping the rabies virus in its tracks before it can jump to humans.

question: What do we call an opportunistic infection?

options.A: A severe infection that only affects individuals over the age of sixty-five
options.B: An illness caused by bacteria that cannot survive outside a host body
options.C: An infection caused by normal flora when the host's defenses are weakened
options.D: A disease spread exclusively through contaminated hospital water supplies

explanation: Think of it this way: normal microbes are usually peaceful neighbours, but if your immune system gets weak, they 'take the opportunity' to cause trouble and sickness.

question: Which insect spreads the malaria parasite to humans?

options.A: Housefly
options.B: Female Anopheles mosquito
options.C: Tsetse fly
options.D: Male Culex mosquito

explanation: Spot on! Malaria is transmitted specifically when an infected female Anopheles mosquito bites looking for a blood meal.

question: What amount of blood loss after a normal vaginal delivery is considered a primary postpartum haemorrhage (PPH)?

options.A: Exceeding 500 mL
options.B: Exceeding 1,500 mL
options.C: Exceeding 250 mL
options.D: Exceeding 1,000 mL

explanation: Primary PPH means losing more than 500 mL of blood within the first 24 hours after a vaginal birth. Keep this number in mind—it's a vital clinical milestone!

question: Why is getting the community involved so important during an outbreak?

options.A: It ensures that international donors send financial aid instantly
options.B: It eliminates the need for any laboratory testing or clinical staff
options.C: It completely stops the replication cycle of bacteria and viruses
options.D: It builds trust and prevents resistance or hiding of sick family members

explanation: When people trust nurses and understand what's going on, they cooperate openly and report sickness early instead of hiding it.

question: You want to learn the latest wound care practices for your clinicals. How can a professional organization help you with this?

options.A: Direct supervision of the nurse during clinical dressing changes
options.B: Access to peer-reviewed professional journals and research
options.C: Immediate financial grants for personal housing and transport
options.D: Free medical supplies delivered directly to the hospital ward

explanation: Professional bodies regularly publish journals filled with fresh, evidence-based research so you can easily keep your clinical skills up to date.

question: Why is it super important for a nurse researcher to clearly define their study population?

options.A: It ensures that every person in the country gets surveyed
options.B: It eliminates all possible errors in data collection
options.C: It reduces the financial cost of printing research papers
options.D: It helps them know exactly who the final study results will apply to

explanation: Spot on! When you know your exact population, you can proudly say who your findings will help in everyday hospital or community practice.

question: What is the medical term for a testicle that fails to move down into the scrotum?

options.A: Cryptorchidism
options.B: Hypospadias
options.C: Phimosis
options.D: Hydrocele

explanation: Cryptorchidism simply means the testicle didn't make the normal journey down into the scrotum before birth. You are doing great mastering these terms!

question: Why is talking to a witness so helpful when assessing a seizure?

options.A: Witnesses can prescribe the right medication immediately
options.B: The patient is usually unable to remember or describe the event themselves
options.C: Witnesses know the exact medical history of the patient
options.D: Doctors do not trust tests like the EEG

explanation: Since patients are often blanking out or unconscious during a fit, someone who watched it happen is your best source for piecing together what really went down!

question: What does reproductive health cover according to standard health definitions?

options.A: Only the ability to bear children without medical complications
options.B: The prevention of sexually transmitted diseases in teenagers
options.C: The total absence of any infection in the pelvic organs
options.D: Complete physical, mental, and social well-being in all reproductive matters

explanation: Reproductive health is a broad state of complete well-being, not merely the absence of disease or infirmity in reproductive organs. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h1)

question: What happens if a patient uses over-the-counter medicated nasal sprays for too many days in a row?

options.A: Rebound nasal congestion
options.B: Severe fungal ear infections
options.C: Systemic high blood pressure
options.D: Permanent loss of the sense of smell

explanation: Exactly! Overusing these sprays causes the blood vessels in the nose to swell right back up even worse once the drug wears off.

question: What is the main difference between acute and chronic pain?

options.A: Acute pain is tied to recent tissue injury and resolves with healing, while chronic pain lasts long past the normal healing period.
options.B: Acute pain can be measured with scales, but chronic pain cannot be measured.
options.C: Acute pain requires no medical treatment, whereas chronic pain requires surgery.
options.D: Acute pain only affects internal organs, while chronic pain only affects the skin and muscles.

explanation: Think of acute pain as a sudden alarm bell that stops when healing happens, while chronic pain sticks around long after the injury has healed.

question: A patient recovering from abdominal surgery has not passed gas or had a bowel movement in three days. Which basic need is primarily affected?

options.A: Elimination
options.B: Safety and security
options.C: Love and belonging
options.D: Self-esteem

explanation: Bowel function falls under physiological elimination needs, which nurses closely monitor post-operatively. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h3)

question: Where does fertilization of an egg by a sperm normally happen?

options.A: Uterine cavity
options.B: Surface of the ovary
options.C: Fallopian tube
options.D: Vaginal canal

explanation: Correct! The sperm and egg usually meet and fuse right there in the fallopian tube on their journey.

question: What quick bedside test helps confirm if a skin rash is caused by a fungus?

options.A: Gram stain of blood cultures
options.B: Complete blood cell count
options.C: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.D: Potassium hydroxide (KOH) wet mount

explanation: Spot on! Adding KOH melts away the skin cells while leaving the stubborn fungal threads clearly visible under a microscope.

question: Which of these is NOT a barrier to good communication between hospital departments?

options.A: Use of specialized professional jargon
options.B: Physical distance between separate hospital units
options.C: Universal and open departmental transparency
options.D: Rigid hierarchy and power dynamics

explanation: Exactly! Transparency actually builds trust and helps communication flow. Things like heavy jargon, long distances, and strict hierarchies are the real roadblocks.

question: Why is regular cleaning and disinfecting of bed accessories so important in the ward?

options.A: To keep the equipment looking brand new for visitors
options.B: To make the rubber and plastic components softer
options.C: To prevent the metal parts from rusting too quickly
options.D: To prevent the spread of hospital-acquired infections

explanation: Spot on! Since bed accessories are often shared, wiping them down thoroughly between patients stops germs from spreading and keeps everyone safe.

question: How do the kidneys respond when the blood becomes too acidic?

options.A: By retaining hydrogen ions and excreting bicarbonate
options.B: By secreting hydrogen ions and reabsorbing bicarbonate
options.C: By slowing down the filtration rate of the glomerulus
options.D: By increasing the production of red blood cells

explanation: You're doing great! To balance the pH, the kidneys pump out extra acid (hydrogen ions) in the urine and keep helpful buffers like bicarbonate in the blood.

question: What measurement does the abbreviation 'mg' stand for?

options.A: Microgram
options.B: Milligram
options.C: Milliliter
options.D: Millimeter

explanation: Easy and correct! 'mg' is the standard metric shortcut for milligram, which you'll see constantly for solid pills and capsules.

question: How does your skin help cool you down on a very hot day?

options.A: By constricting surface blood vessels to trap heat
options.B: By shedding the outer epidermal layer to release trapped heat
options.C: By increasing subcutaneous fat thickness to block external warmth
options.D: By producing sweat and widening blood vessels near the surface

explanation: You've got this! Sweat cools you as it evaporates, and widening your blood vessels lets warm blood flow close to the surface so heat can escape.

question: What is the standard first-line oral antibiotic for treating non-severe pneumonia in under-fives?

options.A: Amoxicillin
options.B: Ciprofloxacin
options.C: Vancomycin
options.D: Tetracycline

explanation: Amoxicillin is the go-to first-line oral treatment for uncomplicated pneumonia because it safely and effectively fights common chest infections.

question: How does the daily work of a PHC nurse differ mainly from a nurse in a high-tech hospital ICU?

options.A: The hospital nurse spends most of their time farming and digging boreholes
options.B: The PHC nurse focuses heavily on community outreach, health promotion, and preventive education
options.C: The PHC nurse is forbidden from touching patients or administering medications
options.D: The PHC nurse only provides end-of-life care and palliative treatments

explanation: Well done! While hospital nurses focus heavily on treating acute illness, PHC nurses focus on keeping the wider community well through prevention and health education.

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to prevent medication errors?

options.A: Minimizing hallway conversations while calculating doses
options.B: Double-checking high-alert calculations with a colleague
options.C: Carefully reading medication labels three separate times
options.D: Rushing through drug rounds to finish ahead of schedule

explanation: Spot on! Rushing causes stress and mistakes. Taking your time is key to safe medication administration.

question: A patient with advanced ovarian cancer just had surgery to remove the tumor masses. What is usually the next step in her care?

options.A: Long-term antibiotic therapy for infection
options.B: Immediate hormone replacement therapy
options.C: Platinum-based combination chemotherapy
options.D: Radiation therapy to the entire brain

explanation: You've got it! After surgery clears out the big masses, systemic chemotherapy helps hunt down any remaining microscopic cancer cells.

question: Which finding in a new mother's lochia (postnatal discharge) should worry you the most?

options.A: A foul or offensive odor coming from the discharge
options.B: A slight increase in flow when the mother stands up
options.C: Small dark clots passed during the first three days
options.D: A gradual fading from red to pink over two weeks

explanation: Lochia naturally changes color and has a normal earthy smell, but a foul odor is a major sign of a uterine infection (endometritis) that needs quick treatment.

question: How many copies of a mutated gene must a child inherit to show symptoms of an autosomal recessive condition?

options.A: Two copies, one from each parent
options.B: Only one copy from the father
options.C: Four copies from extended family
options.D: Only one copy from the mother

explanation: Autosomal recessive disorders require both parents to pass on a copy of the altered gene for the child to be affected. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h2)
