question: What is the main purpose of routine spirometry testing in an industrial occupational health clinic?

options.A: To test the employee's hearing capacity against machine noise
options.B: To check if the worker has contracted a stomach ulcer
options.C: To measure the exact body weight and fat percentage of workers
options.D: To detect early drops in lung function before symptoms appear

explanation: Regular spirometry allows nurses and occupational health officers to spot early breathing impairments so corrective safety steps can be taken immediately. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h8)

question: What is the main goal of teaching female patients about normal bodily transitions?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any future clinic visits
options.B: To convince every woman to use hormone replacement therapy
options.C: To reduce anxiety and clear up common myths about bodily changes
options.D: To prove that menstrual discomfort is purely psychological

explanation: Knowledge is comforting! When women understand their bodies, it eases unnecessary worries and helps them ignore old market myths or village misconceptions.

question: What is the main reason for doing passive range of motion exercises on a bedbound patient?

options.A: To directly build large muscle mass in the limbs
options.B: To prevent joint contractures and maintain flexibility
options.C: To cure underlying systemic cardiovascular disease
options.D: To eliminate the need for any future physical therapy

explanation: You've got this! Moving joints gently keeps them from getting stiff and locked up when patients can't move themselves.

question: When does a patient maintain a stable body weight?

options.A: Energy intake equals energy expenditure
options.B: Energy intake drops to zero for a day
options.C: Energy intake exceeds energy expenditure
options.D: Energy expenditure is higher than energy intake

explanation: Weight remains stable when the total calories consumed match the total calories burned by the body. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h1)

question: What does it mean for a research problem to be measurable?

options.A: The results can be guessed without collecting any data
options.B: Every patient in the hospital must agree with the findings
options.C: Its concepts can be clearly quantified using valid tools or scales
options.D: It can be measured using a simple household ruler

explanation: A measurable problem means you can use clear tools, scores, or observations to track and analyze your study variables accurately.

question: What is a key trait of emotional intelligence in a nurse leader?

options.A: Advanced surgical suturing speed
options.B: Strict adherence to financial auditing
options.C: Physical endurance during night shifts
options.D: Empathy and self-awareness

explanation: You got it! Emotional intelligence is all about understanding your own emotions and tuning into the feelings of those around you.

question: Which pelvic shape is the best and most normal for a smooth vaginal delivery?

options.A: Android
options.B: Platypelloid
options.C: Gynecoid
options.D: Anthropoid

explanation: The gynecoid pelvis is the classic female shape—nice, rounded, and roomy, making it ideal for childbirth!

question: Which group is a primary target for specialized nutritional support programs?

options.A: International food export companies
options.B: Wealthy corporate business owners
options.C: Commercial grain transport drivers
options.D: Pregnant women and young children

explanation: Maternal and child health depends heavily on proper nutrition during critical developmental windows. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h6)

question: Around how many axes of movement does a standard elbow (hinge) joint move?

options.A: Nonaxial
options.B: Biaxial
options.C: Uniaxial
options.D: Multiaxial

explanation: You're doing great! A hinge joint only moves back and forth around one axis (uniaxial), just like a door hinge.

question: What is one of the best long-term ways to improve maternal health in developing countries?

options.A: Relying entirely on traditional birth attendants
options.B: Improving female education and socio-economic empowerment
options.C: Banning family planning services
options.D: Closing all primary health clinics in rural zones

explanation: Educating and empowering women changes everything! When women have a voice and education, they make healthier choices and access care much earlier.

question: Why do nurse-midwives treat every pregnancy as a condition that needs careful monitoring?

options.A: Because it is an inherently pathological state that always causes injury
options.B: Because traditional birth attendants cannot manage normal deliveries
options.C: Because government regulations mandate strict hospital confinement
options.D: Because normal physiological processes can carry unpredictable risks

explanation: Even when a mum is glowing and healthy, things can change quickly. Staying watchful helps us catch any sudden surprises early!

question: Which cells in the pancreas make insulin?

options.A: Beta cells
options.B: Acinar cells
options.C: Delta cells
options.D: Alpha cells

explanation: Spot on! Beta cells in the pancreas are the ones responsible for producing insulin to bring your blood sugar down.

question: What exactly is a lactocele?

options.A: A milk-filled cyst formed from a blocked duct
options.B: An acute bacterial infection of the milk glands
options.C: A normal physiological swelling during milk let-down
options.D: A malignant tumor common in postpartum women

explanation: A lactocele is simply a pocket containing trapped milk that forms when a duct stays blocked. You're doing great!

question: What is the primary advantage of giving medications through the oral route?

options.A: It bypasses liver metabolism completely
options.B: It is the most convenient and common way
options.C: It guarantees 100 percent drug absorption
options.D: It works faster than intravenous injections

explanation: The oral route is favored because patients can usually swallow pills themselves, making it easy and convenient for long-term care. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h1)

question: A patient is due for their blood pressure medication, but their current BP is down to 85/50 mmHg. What should you do first?

options.A: Hold the medication and notify the physician
options.B: Give the drug with a large glass of water
options.C: Proceed with the dose as ordered on the chart
options.D: Administer half the dose to be safe

explanation: Their blood pressure is already on the lower side! Giving a BP-lowering drug now could cause dangerous crashing, so hold the dose and tell the doctor.

question: Why don't patients feel immediate symptom relief right after starting antithyroid medication?

options.A: Body tissues require time to build resistance against excess circulating hormones
options.B: The liver takes at least two weeks to activate the chemical structure of the drug
options.C: The thyroid gland stores large amounts of preformed hormone that must be used up first
options.D: Digestive enzymes in the stomach destroy the medication during the first fortnight

explanation: Think of the thyroid like a full warehouse. It has to clear out its stored hormones before the patient starts feeling better!

question: Which Nigerian agency handles drug law enforcement, arresting traffickers, and seizing illegal substances?

options.A: National Drug Law Enforcement Agency
options.B: Nigerian Communications Commission
options.C: Federal Ministry of Agriculture
options.D: National Youth Service Corps

explanation: The NDLEA is Nigeria's main federal body tasked with tackling drug trafficking and enforcing drug control laws.

question: Why is the pelvis of a young adolescent girl usually not ready for childbirth?

options.A: It lacks adequate muscle attachment
options.B: It expands beyond normal size during puberty
options.C: It is still growing and not fully developed
options.D: It calcifies too early in childhood

explanation: An adolescent's pelvis hasn't reached full growth yet, which causes major physical blocks and dangers during delivery.

question: What main factor helps doctors decide whether to use surgery or radiation for cervical cancer?

options.A: The clinical stage of the cancer and patient health status
options.B: The patient's personal preference for herbal remedies
options.C: The availability of blood donors in the local hospital ward
options.D: The exact blood type of the individual diagnosed

explanation: Exactly! Early stages are often fixed with surgery, while more advanced stages need a mix of radiation and drugs.

question: What is the best nursing approach for a patient with a normal Pap smear and an asymptomatic cervical ectropion?

options.A: Scheduling immediate cryotherapy to freeze the red area off
options.B: Administering a course of strong oral antibiotics
options.C: Advising strict bed rest in the Trendelenburg position
options.D: Providing reassurance and explaining that the condition is often normal

explanation: If the patient feels fine and her Pap smear is clear, no treatment is needed! Your best tool here is kind, reassuring education to let her know her body is doing just fine.

question: A patient insists that their mother, who passed away years ago, is coming to visit today. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Argue firmly that the mother is dead to teach them reality
options.B: Scold the family members for not correcting the patient's false memory
options.C: Ignore the comment completely and pretend you did not hear anything
options.D: Acknowledge the feeling behind the statement and gently redirect their attention

explanation: Argueing causes distress. Instead, validate their emotion ('You really miss your mum, don't you?') and gently steer their focus elsewhere.

question: Why do researchers often recruit more people than their minimum calculated sample size?

options.A: To increase the chance of getting statistically insignificant results
options.B: To account for participants who drop out or withdraw during the study
options.C: To satisfy hospital administrators who love large group numbers
options.D: To make the data entry process longer for student assistants

explanation: Exactly! People travel, fall ill, or change their minds. Adding a buffer upfront saves your project if participants drop out.

question: A patient in her second trimester feels the baby move for the first time and feels much more connected. What is this milestone called?

options.A: Quickening
options.B: Nesting
options.C: Ambivalence
options.D: Couvade

explanation: Well done! Quickening is that magical moment when fetal movement makes the pregnancy feel truly real.

question: Why must you strictly tell a patient who just had transsphenoidal surgery NOT to blow their nose?

options.A: It triggers terrible allergic reactions to the nasal packing materials.
options.B: It pushes air into the ear tubes and causes permanent deafness.
options.C: It increases pressure inside the head and can ruin the surgical seal.
options.D: It causes too much mucus to form and blocks the sinus completely.

explanation: Blowing your nose spikes intracranial pressure. That sudden pressure can pop the tissue patch the surgeon placed over the surgical site, causing cerebrospinal fluid to leak out.

question: What type of language should a nurse use when writing home care notes?

options.A: Brief and casual phrases to save time
options.B: Objective, specific, and measurable details
options.C: General summaries and personal opinions
options.D: Emotional descriptions of the family dynamic

explanation: You got it! Stick to clear, factual observations so any other nurse reading your notes knows the exact status of the patient.

question: Why are nurses often the best healthcare workers to spot early signs of poor nutrition?

options.A: Nurses prepare all the meals served in the hospital
options.B: They spend the most direct time with patients
options.C: Dietitians are not allowed to speak directly with patients
options.D: They are the only staff trained in human metabolism

explanation: Nurses have continuous contact with patients, giving them ample opportunity to observe eating habits and appetite changes firsthand. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h4)

question: A client comes back complaining of mild spotting a month after getting an implant. How should you respond?

options.A: Tell her she has a serious pelvic infection
options.B: Take out the implant immediately and offer nothing else
options.C: Reassure her that this is a normal and common side effect
options.D: Tell her to stop drinking water for two days

explanation: Spot on! Pre-counseling helps clients stay calm. Reassuring them that spotting is normal builds great trust and keeps them comfortable.

question: Why does the body need micronutrients if they are only required in small amounts?

options.A: They are the main source of immediate cellular energy.
options.B: They supply the primary bulk materials for muscle growth.
options.C: They replace the need for drinking water.
options.D: They control metabolic pathways and protect body systems.

explanation: Even though we need them in tiny amounts, vitamins and minerals act like master keys that keep our chemical reactions and body systems running smoothly!

question: What symptom makes vitamin B12 deficiency different from simple iron deficiency?

options.A: Elevation in total white blood cell counts
options.B: Severe swelling in the lower extremities
options.C: Presence of neurological symptoms like numbness
options.D: Rapid drop in liver enzyme production

explanation: B12 protects our nerves! When it's missing, patients can experience tingling or numbness in their hands and feet, which doesn't happen in plain iron deficiency.

question: Why must an unconscious patient be turned to their side before you clean their mouth?

options.A: To help relax the jaw so the mouth opens much wider
options.B: To push more blood straight into the gum tissues
options.C: To stop accidental choking or fluid entering the lungs
options.D: To make it easier to pull out shaky lower teeth

explanation: Safety first! Side-lying lets liquids drain safely out of the mouth instead of pooling in the throat and slipping down into the windpipe.

question: In traditional Nigerian society, who has mainly taken care of older adults needing support?

options.A: Government-run hospitals
options.B: Non-profit religious charities
options.C: Extended family networks
options.D: Private nursing homes

explanation: You got this! Culturally, our extended family system has always been the primary safety net for caring for our aging loved ones.

question: What is the primary function of the innermost layer, the tunica intima?

options.A: Anchoring major blood vessels securely to nearby skeletal bones
options.B: Supplying oxygenated blood directly to the thick outer muscle layers
options.C: Generating rhythmic electrical impulses to contract the vessel wall
options.D: Providing a frictionless endothelial surface for smooth blood flow

explanation: The tunica intima features a slick endothelial lining that reduces cellular friction and prevents unwanted clotting inside healthy vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the best first step when you notice an outlier in your research data?

options.A: Ignore it completely because outliers never matter in research
options.B: Investigate it for potential recording errors or unique clinical cases
options.C: Delete the point immediately to make the graph look cleaner
options.D: Change the scale of the axis so the point disappears

explanation: Always check if it's just a typing mistake, or if it's an exciting, unusual patient case worth noting! Don't just delete data blindly.

question: Where is the best place on the body to give an emergency intramuscular shot of epinephrine?

options.A: Dorsal gluteal muscle
options.B: Anterolateral thigh
options.C: Deltoid muscle of the arm
options.D: Subcutaneous abdominal fat

explanation: Spot on! The outer-front part of the thigh (anterolateral thigh) absorbs medications into the bloodstream much faster and more reliably than other sites.

question: Which of these is NOT a reason why some families might hide a sick relative from home care providers?

options.A: Belief that family care is a strict moral obligation
options.B: Stigma associated with certain chronic or mental illnesses
options.C: Fear of community gossip and social judgment
options.D: Desire to follow strict hospital discharge protocols

explanation: Well done! Families might hide patients due to fear of gossip or stigma, but hospital protocols are never the reason.

question: A 65-year-old worker with long-term chemical exposure comes in with tiredness. Which background factor makes you suspect a blood issue?

options.A: The geographical location of the local grocery store
options.B: The patient's marital status and living arrangements
options.C: The patient's preferred method of daily transportation
options.D: Occupational chemical exposure linked to bone marrow problems

explanation: Workplace exposure to chemicals like benzene can damage the bone marrow and lead to blood issues over time. Always ask about your patients' jobs!

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation in a BCC program?

options.A: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.B: Evaluation happens before the project starts, and monitoring never happens
options.C: There is no difference; both words mean exactly the same thing
options.D: Monitoring is ongoing during the project, while evaluation measures final impact

explanation: Think of monitoring as checking your progress while running the race, and evaluation as looking at your overall performance and medals when the race is finished. You've got this distinction down!

question: Why should a nurse give written discharge instructions about pain meds to a recovering patient?

options.A: It replaces the need for any verbal conversation entirely
options.B: Written papers are legally required to keep nurses from being sued
options.C: Patients often forget verbal instructions due to stress and fatigue
options.D: Pharmacies will not sell pain medication without hospital paper

explanation: When people are stressed or tired, details slip their minds. Written guides are lifesavers for safe home care!

question: What is the largest and least compressible part of the foetal body during birth?

options.A: The shoulders
options.B: The trunk
options.C: The head
options.D: The pelvis

explanation: The foetal skull is the largest part of the infant body and requires careful passage through the pelvis during delivery. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T11#GNS121_U6_T11_h1)

question: Why must patients finish all their antiprotozoal medication even after feeling better?

options.A: Incomplete courses cause permanent damage to human taste buds
options.B: Leftover pills lose their chemical stability and become poisonous
options.C: Health clinics charge heavy fines for unfinished medicine bottles
options.D: Stopping early can leave surviving parasites and cause a relapse

explanation: Amazing work! Feeling better doesn't mean all parasites are gone. Finishing the dose ensures the infection won't bounce back.

question: Why must the bowel be completely cleared before a diagnostic colonoscopy?

options.A: To stimulate the pancreas to produce more digestive enzymes
options.B: To absorb any remaining local anesthetic used in the operating room
options.C: To prevent the patient from feeling hungry during the procedure
options.D: To give the physician a clear, unobstructed view of the intestinal lining

explanation: A clean colon lets the doctor clearly spot polyps, redness, or tiny lesions without stool blocking the way.

question: What is the primary medical treatment used to clear up endometritis?

options.A: Hormone replacement
options.B: Diuretics
options.C: Antibiotics
options.D: Anticonvulsants

explanation: Keep it simple: endometritis is caused by bacteria, so the main cure is giving the right course of antibiotics to wipe them out!

question: How does desmopressin help patients with mild haemophilia A or von Willebrand disease?

options.A: It replaces vitamin K stores directly in the liver.
options.B: It destroys abnormal platelets in the bloodstream.
options.C: It stimulates the release of stored clotting factors from vessel walls.
options.D: It dissolves dangerous clots blocking major blood vessels.

explanation: Desmopressin gives the body a helpful nudge, telling the blood vessels to release extra stored clotting factors so the blood can clot better.

question: Which facility feature helps reduce embarrassment for teenagers visiting a health clinic?

options.A: Waiting areas shared only with elderly patients
options.B: Placing consultation rooms next to the main entrance
options.C: Dedicated youth corners or separate waiting spaces
options.D: Strict formal dress codes for all visitors

explanation: Separate spaces help adolescents feel less exposed and much more comfortable hanging out among their peers.

question: Which of these is the most common reason a patient needs skull traction?

options.A: Degenerative arthritis of the lumbar spine
options.B: Bacterial meningitis with high fever
options.C: Severe chronic tension headaches
options.D: Cervical spine fractures and dislocations

explanation: Spot on! Traction is specifically built to handle broken bones and bad misalignments right in the neck area.

question: Which of these is a common physical sign of andropause?

options.A: Complete sterility
options.B: Severe ovarian atrophy
options.C: Increased visceral fat
options.D: Permanent voice deepening

explanation: As testosterone dips, men often notice changes in their body shape, such as building up a bit more belly fat and losing some muscle firmness.

question: What is the core idea behind cultural competence in nursing?

options.A: Refusing to treat patients who consult traditional healers
options.B: Speaking only English during all patient health education sessions
options.C: Forcing patients to abandon their native beliefs in favor of modern science
options.D: Respecting patient traditions while promoting safe and effective health practices

explanation: Exactly! Cultural competence means honoring where our patients come from and blending their values with safe, evidence-based nursing care.

question: Why do we bother doing nursing research in the first place?

options.A: To increase hospital funding through grants
options.B: To replace traditional nursing duties with laboratory tasks
options.C: To bridge the gap between clinical theory and bedside practice
options.D: To reduce the number of nursing staff needed on wards

explanation: Spot on! Research isn't just for textbooks; it directly helps us connect what we learn in class to giving better, safer care to our patients at the bedside.

question: Why does relaxing the muscle around the airways make breathing easier?

options.A: It increases airway radius and lowers resistance to airflow
options.B: It stops the lungs from producing excess fluid
options.C: It completely cures chronic lung inflammation
options.D: It strengthens the diaphragm muscle during inhalation

explanation: Think of a garden hose: when you relax a tight squeeze, the pipe opens up and water flows smoothly. It's the same idea for air flowing into the lungs!

question: Which of these is a common symptom of the genitourinary syndrome of menopause?

options.A: Excessive facial hair growth
options.B: Vaginal dryness and painful intercourse
options.C: Uncontrolled weight gain in the abdomen
options.D: Permanent loss of bladder sensation

explanation: Low estrogen makes the vaginal tissues thinner and drier, causing discomfort. Knowing this helps us care for patients with empathy.

question: Why do esophageal varices develop in patients with portal hypertension?

options.A: Blood backs up and forces open alternative collateral channels connecting portal and systemic veins
options.B: High stomach acid burns through the protective mucosal barrier of the esophagus
options.C: Swallowed food scraps scrape against the lining of the stomach and damage blood vessels
options.D: The liver releases excess clotting factors that clog small blood vessels near the throat

explanation: When the main gateway to the liver is blocked by high pressure, blood looks for alternative escape routes. It forces open smaller, fragile veins around the esophagus, causing them to bulge out like balloons (varices).

question: How do poor food supply systems directly impact clinical nursing practice?

options.A: By forcing nurses to work directly as agricultural extension officers
options.B: By completely eliminating the need for hospital admission records
options.C: By reducing the total number of patients seeking emergency care
options.D: By increasing cases of malnutrition and diet-related illnesses

explanation: Inadequate food systems lead directly to health conditions like malnutrition and chronic diseases that nurses treat in clinical settings. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h1)

question: Besides jail time and fines, what other financial penalty can a court force a convicted abuser to pay?

options.A: Free housing construction for the entire community
options.B: Compensation payments to the victim for medical and rehabilitation costs
options.C: Full funding of government infrastructure projects
options.D: Mandatory donations to international sports federations

explanation: Spot on! Judges can order perpetrators to pay compensation to help survivors cover their hospital bills and recovery costs.

question: In conservative communities, how is family honor often tied to female family members?

options.A: Through their ability to generate personal business wealth
options.B: Through their athletic achievements in school
options.C: Through their election into local political office
options.D: Through their perceived sexual purity and chastity

explanation: That's right. Traditional communities unfortunately place the heavy burden of family reputation squarely on the sexual purity and behavior of women and girls.

question: Why is checking for gender-based vulnerabilities important during a nursing assessment?

options.A: Social power imbalances directly influence treatment adherence and safety
options.B: Biological sex markers change entirely based on household income
options.C: Hospitals require this data solely for administrative billing records
options.D: Cultural expectations have no bearing on physical healing rates

explanation: You got it! Understanding domestic power dynamics and financial pressures helps us see why a patient might struggle to follow their treatment plan.

question: How is an 'accessible population' different from a 'target population'?

options.A: much larger and broader than the original target group
options.B: exempt from standard hospital ethical clearance procedures
options.C: composed entirely of medical doctors rather than everyday patients
options.D: physically available and realistic for the researcher to recruit

explanation: Spot on! The target group is your dream group, but the accessible group is the practical batch of patients you can actually walk up to and recruit in your hospital.

question: What is the best way to prevent accidental poisoning in community health?

options.A: Building specialized intensive care units in every village clinic
options.B: Educating families on proper chemical storage and prohibiting food-container reuse
options.C: Training traditional healers to perform emergency gastric lavage
options.D: Banning the sale of all cleaning agents and agricultural chemicals

explanation: Correct! Teaching families how to safely store items and never use old drink bottles for chemicals stops poisonings before they happen.

question: How does severe postpartum anaemia commonly impact a new mother in the weeks following discharge?

options.A: It causes permanent high blood pressure requiring daily meds
options.B: It boosts her physical energy due to fast red blood cell recycling
options.C: It speeds up the return of her monthly periods within a week
options.D: It causes deep, persistent fatigue that makes newborn care and bonding tough

explanation: Low haemoglobin means less oxygen travels to her tissues, leaving her utterly exhausted. Supporting her nutrition and recovery is a huge part of postpartum nursing care!

question: Who makes up the control group in a case-control study?

options.A: People who refuse to participate
options.B: People with the disease
options.C: People without the disease
options.D: People currently receiving treatment

explanation: You nailed it! The control group acts as our healthy comparison baseline so we can see what was different about the people who got sick.

question: A nurse wants to test if a new wound dressing heals ulcers faster. What would be the alternative hypothesis?

options.A: The new dressing has no effect on ulcer healing time
options.B: Ulcer healing is entirely unrelated to dressings
options.C: All dressings heal ulcers at the exact same rate
options.D: The new dressing changes the healing time of ulcers

explanation: The alternative hypothesis is what you actually suspect will happen—that there is a real difference or relationship!

question: How does carbon monoxide poisoning cause internal suffocation?

options.A: It directly paralyzes the diaphragm muscle
options.B: It triggers immediate swelling of the vocal cords
options.C: It causes the lungs to fill with fluid rapidly
options.D: It binds to hemoglobin and blocks oxygen delivery

explanation: Carbon monoxide is sneaky—it loves sticking to your red blood cells (hemoglobin) way more than oxygen does. Even if the patient is breathing fine, their tissues still starve because the seats on the transport truck are all taken!

question: Why do women need to use chemical spermicide along with a diaphragm?

options.A: To lubricate the device for easy insertion
options.B: To immobilize and kill sperm that pass the barrier
options.C: To permanently alter the pH of the cervix
options.D: To prevent the growth of yeast infections

explanation: While the physical cup blocks most sperm, spermicide acts as a backup to kill any little swimmers that might slip past the edges!

question: What is the main goal of a Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in a public hospital?

options.A: To generate heavy commercial profits for the government
options.B: To pay the monthly salaries of all medical doctors
options.C: To provide free medical care for all citizens permanently
options.D: To ensure a continuous supply of essential medicines

explanation: You've got this! A DRF uses money from selling drugs to buy more stock, making sure the pharmacy never runs dry. Simple and effective!

question: What is a key nursing care action for a patient dealing with extreme fatigue from disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: Keeping the patient confined strictly to bed
options.B: Restricting all fluid intake after midday
options.C: Scheduling planned rest periods throughout the day
options.D: Encouraging intense daily marathon training

explanation: Pacing is everything! Balancing daily activities with scheduled rest helps patients conserve their energy without burning out.

question: A relative suddenly gets angry and pulls away during a visit. How should you, as a nurse, view this behavior?

options.A: As a sign that the relative wishes to abandon the patient
options.B: As proof that the relative does not care about the patient
options.C: As a normal reaction during the process of anticipatory grief
options.D: As a personal insult directed at the nursing staff

explanation: Don't take it personally! Anger and withdrawal are just natural ways people react when they are struggling to accept an impending, painful loss.

question: What is the very first thing a nurse educator should do when planning a training program for staff?

options.A: Booking a large hotel conference hall
options.B: Printing out attendance certificates
options.C: Conducting a needs assessment
options.D: Purchasing expensive audiovisual equipment

explanation: Before teaching, you have to ask: what do the nurses actually need to learn? A needs assessment helps find the gaps so the training is super useful.

question: What is the main job of the hypothalamus when you experience stress?

options.A: Slowing down your heart rate so you can fall asleep
options.B: Filtering visual signals coming from your eyes
options.C: Linking emotional triggers to physical stress and hormone responses
options.D: Storing facts you learned during your nursing lectures

explanation: You got it! The hypothalamus connects emotional feelings from the limbic system to physical body changes by triggering hormones and your nervous system.

question: When does the general survey of a patient actually begin?

options.A: After listening to the patient's heart and lungs
options.B: When the blood pressure cuff is inflated
options.C: When writing the final discharge notes
options.D: The moment the nurse first sees the patient

explanation: The general survey starts immediately through observation before any hands-on examination takes place. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h4)

question: What is the most important home safety change to make in the bathroom after an amputation?

options.A: Replacing all porcelain fixtures with plastic ones
options.B: Removing the bathroom door to improve airflow
options.C: Installing grab bars near the toilet and shower
options.D: Painting the bathroom walls a bright, cheerful color

explanation: Wet bathroom floors plus new mobility challenges spell danger. Grab bars and shower seats keep baths safe and independent!

question: Why do maternity nurses need to know baby skull anatomy well?

options.A: It helps assess foetal position and monitor labour progress
options.B: It allows the nurse to calculate the exact date of conception
options.C: It determines whether the mother will need a blood transfusion
options.D: It prevents the need for any internal pelvic examinations

explanation: Spot on! By feeling the landmarks on the baby's head during vaginal exams, you can tell which way the baby is facing and how well labor is moving along.

question: What is another popular name for schistosomiasis?

options.A: River blindness
options.B: Chagas disease
options.C: Snail fever
options.D: Sleeping sickness

explanation: You'll often hear schistosomiasis called 'snail fever' because freshwater snails act as the crucial temporary home where the parasites grow during their life cycle. Great job remembering this!

question: Why shouldn't a nurse rely only on visual physical checks when diagnosing malnutrition?

options.A: Clinical signs only appear after the patient is completely cured
options.B: Laboratory tests are illegal to perform in primary health clinics
options.C: Different nutrient shortages can cause very similar physical signs
options.D: Patients usually hide their physical symptoms from healthcare workers

explanation: Many deficiencies look alike on the outside. That's why we always back up our physical exams with diet histories and lab tests!

question: How much energy does one gram of dietary fat provide compared to carbohydrates?

options.A: Half the amount
options.B: More than double the amount
options.C: The exact same amount
options.D: Four times the amount

explanation: Fats pack a heavy punch, giving about 9 kcal per gram, while carbs and proteins give about 4 kcal. That's why fat is such a great energy storage!

question: What is the main reason a nurse performs a follow-up check after giving medication?

options.A: To ask the patient to sign the hospital billing forms
options.B: To evaluate if the drug is working and watch for side effects
options.C: To remind the doctor when the next shift starts
options.D: To clean up the leftover water cups from the bedside table

explanation: Follow-up monitoring ensures therapeutic effectiveness and catches early signs of adverse reactions. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h7)

question: Roughly how much does a normal, full-term placenta weigh?

options.A: 100 grams
options.B: 1000 grams
options.C: 500 grams
options.D: 250 grams

explanation: Think of it as about 500g—roughly one-sixth of the baby's birth weight! Knowing this helps you spot when a placenta is unusually small or heavy. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h1)

question: Why do severe widowhood practices tend to stick around longer in rural villages than in big cities?

options.A: Urban dwellers do not experience the emotional pain of losing a spouse
options.B: Government laws completely ban all cultural practices inside major cities
options.C: Rural areas maintain stronger adherence to traditional and ancestral beliefs
options.D: Traditional rulers in cities have no authority over family matters

explanation: Closer ties to traditional ways and slower rates of modern education mean older customs are preserved more strongly in villages. Keep learning, you're doing great!

question: At what Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score do doctors usually decide to insert an artificial airway (intubation) to protect the patient?

options.A: 8 or lower
options.B: 12 or lower
options.C: 15 exactly
options.D: 3 only

explanation: Remember the golden rule in trauma: 'less than 8, intubate!' A score of 8 or lower means the patient can no longer protect their own airway.

question: Why do mothers with involved partners tend to have better clinic attendance?

options.A: Hospitals give financial rewards to couples who attend together.
options.B: Mothers refuse to leave the house without a male escort.
options.C: Shared responsibility reduces maternal stress and logistical hurdles.
options.D: Fathers force their wives to visit the doctor daily.

explanation: When partners share the load, going to appointments becomes much easier and less stressful for the mother.

question: What is the main catch or limitation of chemical buffer systems?

options.A: They only bind or release ions temporarily without removing them
options.B: They take days to reach peak chemical effectiveness
options.C: They function exclusively inside the cells of skeletal muscle
options.D: They require active nervous system input to initiate action

explanation: Buffers are great first responders, but they only hold onto excess ions temporarily. To truly get rid of acids or bases, the lungs and kidneys have to step in.

question: Why must the tools used to cut the umbilical cord be strictly sterile?

options.A: To follow trendy hospital equipment rules
options.B: To make the cutting smooth and fast for the midwife
options.C: To keep the scissors from getting stained
options.D: To prevent serious infections like neonatal tetanus

explanation: A newborn's belly button is a direct doorway for germs, so keeping cutting tools sterile is a total lifesaving must!

question: What type of food should make up the biggest part of an adolescent girl's daily energy intake?

options.A: Refined table sugars
options.B: Pure protein powders
options.C: Saturated animal fats
options.D: Complex carbohydrates

explanation: Wonderful! Complex carbs (like yam, brown rice, and beans) give growing teens steady, lasting energy and healthy fiber.

question: What is the primary purpose of doing maternal death reviews in a hospital?

options.A: To reduce the number of patients seeking antenatal care
options.B: To satisfy international funding agencies without changing practice
options.C: To find a junior nurse to blame for an unavoidable accident
options.D: To discover systemic failures and prevent similar future tragedies

explanation: Maternal death reviews are never about witch-hunts. They help the team figure out what went wrong in the system so we can protect mothers next time. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h7)

question: A patient has a stiff, painful knee joint. Which membrane inside the joint is likely failing to produce enough lubricating fluid?

options.A: Cutaneous membrane
options.B: Synovial membrane
options.C: Serous membrane
options.D: Mucous membrane

explanation: Synovial membranes line our movable joints and pump out synovial fluid to keep movements smooth and pain-free.

question: Why is the bedside nurse considered the central link in the healthcare nutrition team?

options.A: They have legal power to prescribe diets
options.B: They do all formal nutrition assessments alone
options.C: They observe daily intake and update the team
options.D: They are the only ones allowed to serve food

explanation: You got it! Because we are always at the bedside, we notice what the patient eats and share that info with the doctors and dietitians.

question: Which injection is routinely given to newborns to prevent bleeding?

options.A: Calcium gluconate
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Vitamin C

explanation: Great job! Babies are born with low vitamin K levels, so this shot protects them from bleeding problems.

question: What do the three classic signs of diabetes—polyuria, polydipsia, and polyphagia—actually mean?

options.A: Frequent headaches, blurred vision, and dizziness
options.B: High blood pressure, rapid heart rate, and fever
options.C: Joint pain, muscle weakness, and skin rashes
options.D: Excessive urination, excessive thirst, and excessive hunger

explanation: Just break down the medical terms: 'uria' relates to urine, 'dipsia' to thirst, and 'phagia' to eating/hunger! Remembering the Greek roots makes nursing terms so much easier.

question: Many Nigerians view illness through both physical and spiritual lenses. How does this affect how they seek healthcare?

options.A: It completely stops people from ever visiting modern health clinics
options.B: It ensures that every disease is cured instantly without medication
options.C: It forces the government to ban all imported pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: It leads many patients to combine traditional healing with orthodox medicine

explanation: When people believe an illness has both physical and spiritual causes, it's very natural for them to seek help from both traditional healers and medical doctors to cover all bases!
